class.name: Box3DMultiMeshRenderer
class.brief_description: Draws every [Box3DBody] child as one [MultiMesh] -- one draw call for any number of bodies.
class.description: Add [Box3DBody] children under this node and they are all drawn as instances of a single mesh, in one draw call, with their transforms taken straight from the solver's tick snapshots (interpolated to render time) and uploaded as one bulk buffer. Nothing per-body runs in script, which is what makes scenes of tens of thousands of bodies practical. [b]All the bodies must share one shape and size[/b], because a [MultiMesh] draws one mesh: the mesh is built from the first child's [member Box3DBody.box_size]. Instances are tinted across a pastel hue range. Bodies drawn this way have their [member Box3DBody.sync_node_transform] turned off, so their node transforms stay at the spawn pose -- read positions from the physics, not from the node.

method.name: get_replay_body_colors
method.description: The colour this node gave each body it draws, as [code]{ Box3DBody: Color }[/code]. A body rendered here has no visual of its own -- this node frees the [MeshInstance3D] it came with -- so its colour exists only in this node's instance buffer, and nothing outside can read it back: [MultiMesh] colours live in the [RenderingServer], which stores none of them in a headless run. So anything that wants to carry these colours somewhere else has to ask, and this is the question. The demo's replay sidecar is the caller: it asks at record-stop and writes the answers beside the recording, which is what lets [member Box3DReplayRenderer.body_color_overrides] bring a replay back looking like the scene that was recorded.
